{"id": "9386a871-f01d-495b-99ef-81d40c1b8510", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Raise it through Service Quotas, or through AWS Support for quotas that can't be adjusted in the console. Check first which kind of limit you're hitting.

**1. Identify the quota**
- The error text tells you which limit it is. "Too many requests" is requests per minute (RPM). "Too many tokens" is tokens per minute (TPM).
- Quotas are per model and per Region. Cross-Region inference profiles (model IDs with a `us.` or `eu.` prefix) have their own separate quotas.
- Some models have fixed quotas that can't be raised.

**2. Request the increase**
- **Quota marked Adjustable = Yes:** In Service Quotas, open the Amazon Bedrock service, find the quota for your model and Region, and choose Request increase.
- **Tokens per minute:** Request an increase on "Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for *your model*". AWS Support will then offer to raise the on-demand TPM and the Cross-Model Max Tokens Per Day quotas together.
- **Quota not adjustable, or the increase is denied:** Open an AWS Support case or contact your account manager.
- Include the quota name, model ID, Region, and your use case. Also include your projected steady and peak RPM and TPM, and your average input and output tokens per request.

**Things that affect approval**
- AWS prioritizes accounts that are already consuming most of their current allocation, so a request can be denied if your usage is low.
- Increases aren't granted for models in Legacy or Deprecated status. Migrate to the successor model instead.
- New accounts often start with lower quotas.

**While you wait**
- Add retries with exponential backoff and jitter. The AWS SDKs can do this for you.
- Use a cross-Region inference profile, which draws on a larger pool of capacity.
- For steady, predictable load, look at Provisioned Throughput. Reserved Tier is available for some models through your account team.

I checked this account's Service Quotas for Bedrock in us-east-1 and my filter returned no InvokeModel quotas. That doesn't show what your limits are. I can also tell you whether the throttling is on requests or tokens.

Sources:
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-runtime.html
- https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-throttling-error
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/troubleshooting-api-error-codes.html", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
